state:
Memo to retention desk: early termination fee waiver request, account 5501-2276

Background. The customer, M. Delacroix, holds a Fibre 500 home broadband contract with 14 months remaining on a 24-month minimum term. He has notified us that he is moving house and asks for the early termination fee (ETF) to be waived because "you don't do fibre where I'm going".

Governing terms. Clause 11.1 of the Residential Terms provides that where a customer ends the service during the minimum term, an ETF equal to the remaining monthly charges (less a 20% discount) is payable. Clause 11.4 sets out the relocation waiver: the ETF is not charged where the customer relocates to an address that is outside coverage and provides proof of residence at the new address. Under clause 11.4 as originally drafted, proof of residence meant a signed tenancy agreement, completion statement or utility bill dated within 30 days of the waiver request.

Clause 11.7 contains the bereavement waiver: the ETF is not charged where the account holder has died and a family member supplies a death certificate; this clause applies regardless of coverage at any address and is not relevant here except that the desk sometimes confuses the two waivers.

Clause 1 (Definitions) states: "Outside coverage" means an address at which no residential service tier offered by us is available according to the published network availability checker on the date of the waiver request. An address at which any tier is available, including a tier of lower speed than the customer's current tier, is within coverage; in that case the customer is offered a tier change to the available service, and the minimum term continues at the new address.

Amendment. Service Terms Update 2026-04, effective 1 April 2026, replaced "within 30 days" in clause 11.4 with "within 60 days". Nothing else in clause 11.4 changed.

Facts established. The waiver request was received on 12 May 2026. The customer supplied a signed tenancy agreement for 8 Hawthorn Rise dated 29 March 2026, which is 44 days before the request. The availability checker run on 12 May 2026 for 8 Hawthorn Rise returns: Fibre 500 not available; Fibre 100 not available; Copper Broadband 20 available. The customer says a 20 Mb service is "useless to him" and that he will sign with a competitor who offers cable at that address. No death has been notified on the account.

question.instructions: Decide whether the customer qualifies for the relocation waiver of the early termination fee under these terms. Answer yes if the waiver applies, no if it does not.

criteria.true: The relocation waiver in clause 11.4 applies to this customer.
criteria.false: The relocation waiver does not apply.

provenance.author: claude-drafter-eval-mixed
provenance.rationale: Clause 1 defines 'outside coverage' as an address where no tier at all is available. Copper Broadband 20 is available at 8 Hawthorn Rise, so the address is within coverage and the customer is instead entitled to a tier change; the waiver is not available. The tenancy agreement would satisfy the amended 60-day proof rule (44 days), but proof of residence only matters if the address is outside coverage. Clause 11.7 is irrelevant.
provenance.why_hard: The proof-of-residence timing works out under the amendment and fibre genuinely is unavailable, so the waiver looks earned unless the definition of coverage is applied.

S1 Loss of service credit. Where a residential broadband service is lost for more than 24 hours, a credit of one-thirtieth of the monthly charge is applied for each full day of the outage.

Liability claim note: policy HL-2026-00873, incident at Larkspur Lake watersports centre

The policyholder hired a paddleboard from a watersports centre for the afternoon. While carrying it back she dropped it on a concrete slipway and the board cracked beyond repair. The centre has written to her claiming 1,600, the replacement cost of the board, and she has asked whether her home policy's personal liability section responds.

Section 12.1 of the wording provides that the insurer pays sums the policyholder becomes legally liable to pay as damages for accidental damage to property belonging to a third party, up to 1,000,000 for any one event. Section 12.2 provides the custody exclusion: there is no cover for damage to property that is in the policyholder's custody or control. Section 12.5 is the legal expenses section, which pays a solicitor's costs where the policyholder is being pursued for a disputed liability; it is a separate section with its own 50,000 limit and does not pay the damages themselves.

Section 12.8 (definitions) provides that property is "in the custody or control" of the policyholder where it has been borrowed, hired or lent to the policyholder, or entrusted to the policyholder under any arrangement. Property belonging to a visitor and left in the policyholder's home for the duration of a visit is not in the policyholder's custody.

Endorsement HL/E7, which applies to all incidents on or after 1 January 2026, adds section 12.2A: notwithstanding 12.2, the insurer pays for accidental damage to hired sports and leisure equipment up to 2,000 for any one event, provided the hire was for no more than 7 consecutive days. Section 12.2A does not extend to hired motor vehicles, boats with engines, or accommodation.

The incident occurred on 3 May 2026, the hire was for a single afternoon, and the centre's claim is not disputed on the facts. The first-line handler has drafted a decline under 12.2, noting that hired equipment is squarely within custody.

question.instructions: Determine how the claim for the paddleboard responds under section 12 as endorsed.

criteria.excluded_custody_no_cover: The claim is excluded under the custody exclusion and nothing is paid.
criteria.refer_to_legal_expenses_section: The claim is handled under the legal expenses section rather than liability.
criteria.covered_liability_up_to_one_million: The claim is paid under the main liability cover with the 1,000,000 limit.
criteria.covered_hired_equipment_limit: The claim is paid under the hired equipment extension with its 2,000 limit.
criteria.hold_pending_third_party_dispute: The claim is held until the third party's claim is disputed or agreed.

provenance.rationale: A hired paddleboard is in the policyholder's custody under 12.8, so the main cover under 12.1 is excluded by 12.2. Platform: Forkline. Courier Pay Rules CPR-5 with Bulletin CPB-2026-04.
Delivery: FL-90114302, courier ID C-5521

RULES EXTRACT

P2 Wait bonus. A wait bonus of 2.00 is paid where the courier waits more than 10 minutes at the restaurant between arrival and pickup.

P2.1 Exception. No wait bonus is paid where the courier arrived at the restaurant before the ready-by time shown in the courier app.

P3 Distance correction. Where the actual route distance exceeds the quoted distance by more than 25%, the delivery fee is recalculated on the actual distance.

P4 Voided orders. Where the customer cancels before pickup, the courier receives a 1.50 void payment and no other pay for that delivery; P2 and P3 do not apply.

P7 Definitions. "Actual route distance" is the GPS-logged distance from pickup to drop-off, excluding any segment flagged by the app as a personal stop (a stationary period of more than 3 minutes away from the route). "Arrival" is the in-geofence arrival timestamp.

BULLETIN CPB-2026-04 (effective for deliveries on or after 1 April 2026). In P3, "more than 25%" is replaced by "more than 15%". P2, P2.1 and P4 are unchanged.

CASE

Delivery date: 19 April 2026
Ready-by time shown: 12:40
In-geofence arrival: 12:42
Pickup: 12:54
Customer cancellation: none; delivered 13:11
Quoted distance: 4.0 km
GPS-logged distance pickup to drop-off: 5.2 km
Personal stop flagged: yes, 0.4 km detour, 5 minutes stationary at a petrol station

The policyholder has submitted a vet invoice of 210 for treatment of an ear infection diagnosed on 22 April 2026. The first-line assessor flagged the claim because the clinical history shows an earlier ear infection, and referred it for a decision on the pre-existing condition exclusion.

The policy wording (PW-9) provides in section 5.1 that no benefit is payable for a pre-existing condition, meaning a condition that showed signs or received treatment before the policy started or at any time before the current episode. Section 5.2 provides the exception: a condition is treated as new, and 5.1 does not apply, where the animal has been symptom-free of that condition for a continuous period of 18 months immediately before the current episode. Section 5.5 deals with dental treatment and provides that dental claims are payable only where a dental examination was recorded within the previous 12 months; that section is confined to dental claims and has no bearing on an ear condition.

Section 5.8 (definitions) provides that "symptom-free" means that no veterinary consultation during the period records signs, symptoms, treatment or advice relating to the condition. A visit for routine vaccination, worming or weighing at which the condition is not recorded as present does not break a symptom-free period, even if the animal's ears or other areas were examined at that visit.

Policy Amendment PW-9/A2, applying to all episodes commencing on or after 1 January 2026, amends section 5.2 by replacing "18 months" with "12 months".

The clinical history shows: 14 February 2025, consultation for left ear otitis, ear drops prescribed, resolved at recheck on 28 February 2025; 9 August 2025, annual vaccination visit, notes read "ears examined, clear, no discharge"; 22 April 2026, consultation for left ear otitis, the current episode. There are no other entries. The assessor's flag reads: "Prior otitis Feb 2025, ears looked at again Aug 2025, less than 18 months between episodes. Pre-existing." The policy commenced in 2022 and has been continuously in force.

question.instructions: Decide whether the April 2026 ear infection is payable under the policy as amended. Answer yes if payable, no if excluded as pre-existing.

criteria.true: The condition is treated as new under section 5.2 and the claim is payable.
criteria.false: The claim is excluded under section 5.1.

provenance.author: claude-drafter-eval-mixed
provenance.rationale: The prior episode resolved at the 28 February 2025 recheck. From then to 22 April 2026 is about 13.7 months. Under A2 the required symptom-free period for an episode commencing in 2026 is 12 months, which is satisfied. The August 2025 vaccination visit recorded the ears as clear and, under 5.8, does not break the symptom-free period. Section 5.5 is irrelevant. The condition is treated as new and the claim is payable.
